newsitem.title: FRANCE: Juppe says wants fair value for euro.
newsitem.headline: Juppe says wants fair value for euro.

text.p: Europe's new single currency must be fairly valued to provide strong employment growth, French Prime Minister Alain Juppe said in a book published on Monday.
"Our German friends say they do not want a "soft euro'. Neither do I. Neither a soft euro nor soft economic growth. I want a "fair euro' in order to have strong employment," he said.

"I insist that these questions must not be left to the judgement of central bank governors alone," he said in "Entre Nous" (Between You and Me), a short book which aims to explain his government's policies to the French people.
"It is essential this vital question is clarified before 1999 and entry to the European currency," he added.

His book was released to the media only days after France and Germany buried their differences over exchange rate policy in order to agree a budget discipline pact meant to underpin the stability of the euro after its launch in 1999.
France and Germany have very different views on exchange rate policy after the launch of the euro.
While Paris wants active management by politicians to push up the value of the dollar, Bonn has insisted on currency stability, underpinned by a fully independent central bank.

Juppe said that he, and President Jacques Chirac, were convinced of the need to create a single currency to give Europe the power to fight against the domination of the dollar and the caprices of financial markets.
